turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Hi. Well, I'm here because I just can't stop thinking about my appearance. It's mostly my hairline, and... the way my face looks under the bright lights at the restaurant where I work. I feel like it makes me look really old and just strange. It's constantly on my mind, even though my coworkers tell me they don't see what I'm talking about when I bring it up.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient explicitly describes a constant preoccupation with perceived defects in their hairline and facial appearance under bright lights, which coworkers state they do not see.

turns.doctor_question: How convinced are you that the problem with your hairline and face is truly there, despite what your coworkers tell you?
turns.patient_response: I'm completely convinced. I mean, I know what I see. When I look in the mirror before my shift, it's... it's right there. I know they say they don't notice it, but I just figure they're being polite, or maybe they just don't want to make me feel bad. But there's absolutely no doubt in my mind. It's real.

turns.doctor_question: Do you repeatedly check, groom, camouflage, or compare your appearance because of these concerns?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I do. Especially before a shift. I'll go into the bathroom and just keep checking the mirror. I take pictures on my phone from all these different angles to see how bad it looks. Then I'll spend I don't know how long trying to comb my hair forward to cover it up. I just keep replaying in my head how the guests are going to see me when I'm standing at the host stand under those lights. I do it so much that half the time I end up being late, or I just get so worked up I can barely bring myself to go out front.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in repetitive behaviors in response to appearance concerns, including repeatedly checking the mirror, taking photos from various angles, and excessively camouflaging by combing their hair forward.

turns.doctor_question: Apart from your concerns about your appearance, do you have any other beliefs that people tell you are not true but that you remain completely certain are true?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't think so. It's really just... just my hairline and my face. I don't have any other beliefs that people disagree with me on, or anything strange like that. It's strictly just about the way I look.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies having any fixed, unusual beliefs or beliefs that others disagree with outside of their appearance concerns.

turns.doctor_question: Is your main belief that you have a specific unacceptable flaw in your appearance, rather than that other people are deliberately reacting to or targeting you because of it?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, that's right. It's really just about the flaw itself. I don't think people are... out to get me, or trying to target me or anything like that. It's not a conspiracy. 

It's just that I know how bad my hairline and my face look. That's the whole issue for me. I just can't stand that I look this way, especially when I have to be the first face people see at the restaurant. But no, I don't think anyone is deliberately coming after me or plotting against me because of it. It's just the fact that the flaw is there.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient confirms their primary issue is distress over a perceived flaw in their physical appearance, specifically focusing on their hairline and face.
symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies persecutory delusions, clarifying that they do not believe people are out to get them, targeting them, or plotting against them.
